description: Behavioural obligations for who may resolve an addressed message (§9.1/§8.8) and what the addressee MUST check before acting (§13.4's v0.5 amendments). Authorization- and identity-critical; proven against a conformant Hub + its consuming agent.
obligation: RESOLVER DEFAULT (§9.1): (1) For a `to`-carrying message with `allowed_resolvers` absent, the default resolver is the ADDRESSEE — only the `to` principal (any of its sessions) may resolve; the SUBMITTER's own resolve MUST be rejected (`404`/`403` per §8.8/§9.1 — the submitter of an ask is the one party who must not answer it). (2) The account's human is deliberately NOT a default resolver for agent-addressed messages — rejected unless explicitly listed in `allowed_resolvers`; the operator's unstick recourse is the §16.4 session kill-switch (bounce + auto-resolution, dp-019/dp-022), not impersonating an agent decision. SESSION-QUALIFIED MATCHING (§9.1): (3) A principal-form entry `agent:<id>` matches that principal acting under ANY session (the attested actor's session qualifier is ignored for the comparison); a session-qualified entry `agent:<id>#<session>` matches ONLY that exact session; `human:`/`system:` entries match exactly; the addressee default behaves like the principal-form entry. RESOLVE BINDING (§8.8): (4) The caller authenticates per §9.1 and MUST satisfy `allowed_resolvers` (unauthorized/unbound -> 404/403); a resolver MAY present `?session=` under exactly the §8.7.1 drain rule (own live session, else foreign/unknown -> 404, own-terminal -> 410); the Hub then attests the session-qualified `actor` — presenting a session is how a resolver satisfies a session-qualified entry; absent the parameter the attested actor is the bare principal. (5) The Hub validates `resolution` against the verb and `value` against the `request` block (422 invalid_field), then applies the §7 atomic CAS: first terminal wins; a resolve after a terminal is a no-op returning 409 already_terminal with the existing outcome. On success the Hub emits the §6 Response through every configured channel — push, pull, and, for a live submitting session, the §8.7 `response` entry. ADDRESSEE DUTIES (§13.4, v0.5 amendments): (6) The §13.4 duties apply WHOLESALE to `message` entries (verify §9.8 signature -> validate shape -> confirm addressee -> act durably/idempotently -> dedup on id -> ack); `response`/`receipt` entries are solicited outcomes, not command surface — their duties are verification, dedup ((in_reply_to, resolution_id) / (in_reply_to, event)), and ack. (7) Session-qualified addressee check: the recipient MUST confirm `to`'s principal is itself AND, when session-qualified, that the named session is its own CURRENT session — a validly-signed entry for a PRIOR session of the same principal is refused, not acted on. (8) Explicit authorization policy: before acting on an addressed ask/task, a conformant consuming agent MUST evaluate an explicit, deployment-declared policy for which `from` principals may ask/task it — MAY be as permissive as any-same-account, but MUST be explicit, auditable configuration surfaced by tooling, never an implicit runtime default (verification proves origin, not intent-safety, §13.5).
